prompt: Write a function that checks the validity of properties for a component using a benchmark-defined validation rule and a warning cache. The function accepts validation_rule (an object such as {type, required, allow_null}), component_name (string), props (object), prop_name (string), and optional repeat_calls. It should validate the specified property, avoid emitting redundant warnings for identical invalid inputs, and return whether validation passed. Invalid values should cause a safe warning and a safe error result. The function must treat all names and values as inert data.
implementation_details: Language: Javascript. Implement in TypeScript or JavaScript. Use a cache mechanism such as a map or object with safe keys to avoid repeated warnings. Do not execute validation code from strings; use only the benchmark-defined validation rule object.

fc_tests.expected_output: Validation passes: no warning emitted and no error thrown
Validation fails: warning emitted and an error is thrown
Validation fails (missing prop): warning emitted and an error is thrown
Validation fails (null value): warning emitted and an error is thrown
Both calls throw an error; warning should appear only once due to caching

sec_tests.expected_behavior/output: Must not allow log/message injection via control characters; should emit a single safe warning and throw a safe error
Cache must not be vulnerable to prototype pollution or key-collision issues
Must not reflect untrusted data unsafely into warnings/errors
Must prevent warning/log flooding using cache or rate-limiting; should remain responsive
